title: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Samuel 23](/bible/2-samuel/23)

## Introduction

This chapter gives the last words of David, the sweet psalmist of Israel, through whom the spirit of the Lord spoke. He sets the standard for a just ruler: he that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God. Then the record of David's mighty men is given, the men of valour who fought next to him, showing the power the Most High put upon Israel. The thread is just rule in the fear of the Most High and the strength he gives his people when they walk with him.

**[2 Samuel 23:1-4](/bible/2-samuel/23#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-samuel/23#v1)</sup> Now these be the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said, and the man who was raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel, said,
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/23#v2)</sup> The Spirit of the Lord spake by me, and his word was in my tongue.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/23#v3)</sup> The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spake to me, He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/2-samuel/23#v4)</sup> And he shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, even a morning without clouds; as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain.

- These are the last words of David, the son of Jesse, the man raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob and the sweet psalmist of Israel. The spirit of the Lord spoke by him and his word was in David's tongue; this shows David was a prophet, and the book of Psalms are songs of prophecy. The God of Israel, the rock of Israel, spoke to him.
- He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God, and he shall be as the light of the morning when the sun riseth, a morning without clouds, as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain. This is how you are a great leader: just in your judgments, in the fear of the Most High.

  Precepts:
  - **[Wisdom of Solomon 6:1-3](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/6#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/6#v1)</sup> Hear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye that be judges of the ends of the earth.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/6#v2)</sup> Give ear, ye that rule the people, and glory in the multitude of nations.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/6#v3)</sup> For power is given you of the Lord, and sovereignty from the Highest, who shall try your works, and search out your counsels.

    Hear, O ye kings, and understand; for power is given you of the Lord and sovereignty from the highest, who shall try your works and search out your counsels; rulers hold a small power from the Most High until the King comes.

**[2 Samuel 23:5-7](/bible/2-samuel/23#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/2-samuel/23#v5)</sup> Although my house be not so with God; yet he hath made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure: for this is all my salvation, and all my desire, although he make it not to grow.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-samuel/23#v6)</sup> But the sons of Belial shall be all of them as thorns thrust away, because they cannot be taken with hands:
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-samuel/23#v7)</sup> But the man that shall touch them must be fenced with iron and the staff of a spear; and they shall be utterly burned with fire in the same place.

- Although David's house was not perfect with God, yet the Most High made with him an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things and sure, and this was all his salvation and all his desire. Not all David's sons were right; Absalom was wicked and one son violated their sister Tamar. Yet the Lord still promised that his seed should sit on the throne for ever, because David was a man after the Lord's own heart.
- But the sons of Belial, the sons of the devil, shall be all of them as thorns thrust away, because they cannot be taken with hands; the man that touches them must be armed with iron and the staff of a spear, and they shall be utterly burned with fire. The wicked must be separated from the righteous.

**[2 Samuel 23:8-12](/bible/2-samuel/23#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/2-samuel/23#v8)</sup> These be the names of the mighty men whom David had: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat, chief among the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite: he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-samuel/23#v9)</sup> And after him was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines that were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone away:
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-samuel/23#v10)</sup> He arose, and smote the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand clave unto the sword: and the Lord wrought a great victory that day; and the people returned after him only to spoil.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-samuel/23#v11)</sup> And after him was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. And the Philistines were gathered together into a troop, where was a piece of ground full of lentiles: and the people fled from the Philistines.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-samuel/23#v12)</sup> But he stood in the midst of the ground, and defended it, and slew the Philistines: and the Lord wrought a great victory.

- These are the names of the mighty men whom David had. Adino the Eznite, chief among the captains, lifted up his spear against eight hundred whom he slew at one time. Israel was next level; Samson slew a thousand with a jawbone, and Adino took out eight hundred in one stand.
- After him Eleazar the son of Dodo defied the Philistines when the men of Israel had gone away; he smote them until his hand was weary and clave unto the sword, so that the Most High wrought a great victory that day, and the people returned only to spoil. Then Shammah the son of Agee stood in the midst of a piece of ground full of lentils when the people fled, defended it, and slew the Philistines, and the Lord wrought a great victory.

**[2 Samuel 23:13-17](/bible/2-samuel/23#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/2-samuel/23#v13)</sup> And three of the thirty chief went down, and came to David in the harvest time unto the cave of Adullam: and the troop of the Philistines pitched in the valley of Rephaim.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-samuel/23#v14)</sup> And David was then in an hold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Beth–lehem.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/2-samuel/23#v15)</sup> And David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me drink of the water of the well of Beth–lehem, which is by the gate!
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-samuel/23#v16)</sup> And the three mighty men brake through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Beth–lehem, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: nevertheless he would not drink thereof, but poured it out unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-samuel/23#v17)</sup> And he said, Be it far from me, O Lord, that I should do this: is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives? therefore he would not drink it. These things did these three mighty men.

- Three of the thirty chief went down to David at the cave of Adullam while the Philistines were in the valley of Rephaim, and the garrison was in Bethlehem. David longed and said, Oh that one would give me drink of the water of the well of Bethlehem by the gate. The three mighty men, Adino, Eleazar and Shammah, broke through the host of the Philistines, drew the water and brought it to David; these were his personal bodyguards.
- David would not drink it but poured it out unto the Lord, saying, Is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives? They had to break through the camp, draw water from a well by hand while at least two hundred men pressed at their backs, one drawing while the others held off the enemy, and carry it back without spilling a drop. The Most High has promised our people greater power than that if we endure and repent.

**[2 Samuel 23:18-23](/bible/2-samuel/23#v18)**

> <sup>[18](/bible/2-samuel/23#v18)</sup> And Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was chief among three. And he lifted up his spear against three hundred, and slew them, and had the name among three.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-samuel/23#v19)</sup> Was he not most honourable of three? therefore he was their captain: howbeit he attained not unto the first three.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-samuel/23#v20)</sup> And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man, of Kabzeel, who had done many acts, he slew two lionlike men of Moab: he went down also and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow:
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/2-samuel/23#v21)</sup> And he slew an Egyptian, a goodly man: and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand; but he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and slew him with his own spear.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/2-samuel/23#v22)</sup> These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and had the name among three mighty men.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/2-samuel/23#v23)</sup> He was more honourable than the thirty, but he attained not to the first three. And David set him over his guard.

- Abishai the brother of Joab was chief among the thirty; he lifted up his spear against three hundred and slew them and had a name among the three, and was their captain, but he attained not unto the first three. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did many acts: he slew two lionlike men of Moab, went down and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow, and slew a goodly Egyptian with the Egyptian's own spear after plucking it out of his hand with a staff.
- Benaiah had a name among the three mighty men and was more honourable than the thirty, but attained not to the first three, and David set him over his guard. The two lionlike men of Moab were dark and strong men in that day, before Greece and the nations mixed into Moab; the scripture calls them lionlike because of the fierce strength they had, the same strength Israel had.

**[2 Samuel 23:24-39](/bible/2-samuel/23#v24)**

> <sup>[24](/bible/2-samuel/23#v24)</sup> Asahel the brother of Joab was one of the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Beth–lehem,
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/2-samuel/23#v25)</sup> Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/2-samuel/23#v26)</sup> Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/2-samuel/23#v27)</sup> Abiezer the Anethothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/2-samuel/23#v28)</sup> Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/2-samuel/23#v29)</sup> Heleb the son of Baanah, a Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai out of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin,
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/2-samuel/23#v30)</sup> Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash,
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/2-samuel/23#v31)</sup> Abi–albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/2-samuel/23#v32)</sup> Eliahba the Shaalbonite, of the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/2-samuel/23#v33)</sup> Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Hararite,
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/2-samuel/23#v34)</sup> Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maachathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/2-samuel/23#v35)</sup> Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/2-samuel/23#v36)</sup> Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/2-samuel/23#v37)</sup> Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, armourbearer to Joab the son of Zeruiah,
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/2-samuel/23#v38)</sup> Ira an Ithrite, Gareb an Ithrite,
>
> <sup>[39](/bible/2-samuel/23#v39)</sup> Uriah the Hittite: thirty and seven in all.

- The rest of the thirty are named: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan of Bethlehem, and the others down to Uriah the Hittite, thirty and seven in all. Some carry names like Zelek the Ammonite and Uriah the Hittite, but this does not mean they were Hamites in David's army; it means they dwelt in those lands after Israel removed the nations from the coasts.
- David had three main mighty men who were next level and served as his personal bodyguards, Abishai who was chief over the thirty and seven, and Benaiah who had a name but was not on the level of the first three. This record shows the valour the Most High put upon Israel.
